Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand the underlying cause, can you tell me if you have experienced recurrent fractures from minor injuries or if your bones bend easily?

Also, have you noticed any short stature, joint hypermobility, or distinctive facial features like a wide mouth or prominent forehead?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (specifically 21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (clitoromegaly/labial fusion), severe acne, hirsutism in the mother, primary amenorrhea, and bone fragility suggests a history of virilization and potential vitamin D deficiency or Cushingoid features. Can you tell me if you have experienced rapid growth spurts during childhood or if you have been diagnosed with high blood pressure or difficulty losing weight despite diet? REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone level, Karyotype.
